A brief history to provide some perspective: McCormick Pier was the first substantial project leading to the conversion of the industrial area north of Burnside, resulting in the creation of what is now called The Pearl District. It is the root of The Pearl’s trunk. In 1979, the Bill Naito Co. acquired the property from Union Pacific. Bill Naito was widely recognized for taking on ventures that were at least as beneficial to the community as they were potentially moneymaking. In 1981 he built the 300-unit McCormick Pier Apartments along the waterfront, replacing a derelict warehouse district and providing needed middle-income housing in an area where other developers had concluded it could not succeed. The company sold the property in 2002 to a developer who successfully converted the apartments into condominiums. Naito Parkway is named for a responsible developer who had a great influence on Portland’s growth into a unique and desirable city. Ref: bit.ly/23xnfC9 Ref: bit.ly/23xnD3L

During an incident or event involving the particular group, a wealth of information can be found. Ultimately, users of non-traditional media go back to traditional media to see what is being reported. This is where professional journalists need to be value-added (filters for what is credible and reliable) rather than value-negative (filters for their own agendas). An accurate and reliable media outlet will always have its place in a functioning society. Media outlets that are value-negative (filtering news for an agenda) are easy to detect these days. If reports are not accurate, reliable or are based on an agenda, people will return to the alternative forum and let it be known.

Second scenario has one person earning $20,000 in year 1 and $150,000 in year 2 while the second person earns $150,000 in year 1 and $20,000 in year two. Income inequality hasn't changed at all, but income stability is vastly decreased. What the study is stating is more about a lack of income stability causing insolvencies, where a person might earn a lot one year and take on a lot of debt but then earn much less in the future, eg. after being laid off, and not be able to afford that debt anymore. Canadian consumers will benefit if the current Supreme Court justices support the trial judge's decision and sweep away all of the barriers to trade among the provinces.

Aircraft flying over land use VHF radio waves to communicate with air traffic control. Pilots change frequency often because the transmitters only cover roughly 60 miles in any direction. In order to stay in contact with air traffic control when flying over areas that don't allow for VHF transmitter placement (like oceans), Aircraft us HF radio. This is because HF radio is skywave propagation, it refracts off the ionosphere to provide over the horizon communication. If the earth where flat, the only transmitter limitation would be the power of the transmitter. If you ever go out in the country and see an extremely tall radio tower, you are looking at proof the earth is round. Your statement about improving the bottom line by not contributing to the plan is incorrect, as accounting rules don't use cash contributions as the expense amount on the company's income statement. Instead the pension expense amount is the future pension amount earned in the current year by the existing employees plus an interest expense on the amount of unfunded pension liability. By having a high deficit in the DB plan the expense on the company's books actually goes up because the interest expense on the deficit is higher, hurting the bottom line. So there is actually an incentive for companies to fund the plan from an income statement point of view. This is totally opposite to what you have said in your post.

2. “To which bulls do you refer?” A bull is a type of public decree issued by a pope, the bishop of Rome. It is named after the leaden seal (bulla) that was traditionally appended to the end in order to authenticate it. Modern scholars have retroactively used the word "bull" to describe any elaborate papal document issued in the form of a decree or privilege, solemn or simple, and to some less elaborate ones issued in the form of a letter. Today, the bull is the only written communication in which the pope will refer to himself as "Episcopus Servus Servorum Dei" ("Bishop, Servant of the Servants of God").
